stem: A 4-year-old with an oesophageal button battery is awaiting theatre 3 hours after ingestion; what honey regimen should be given while waiting?

options.text: 10 mL every 10 minutes, up to 6 doses
5 mL every 30 minutes until symptoms resolve
20 mL once only, then nil by mouth
Give honey only after the battery has passed the oesophagus

explanation: The correct answer is 10 mL every 10 minutes, up to 6 doses. This is the recommended interim honey regimen for a child older than 1 year with an oesophageal button battery within 12 hours of ingestion while awaiting theatre.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf p.142

rationale: The regimen is a time-specific interim measure used before removal of an oesophageal button battery in an appropriate child.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because the recommended interim honey regimen is 10 mL every 10 minutes, up to 6 doses.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because this dose and interval do not match the recommended regimen.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because a single 20 mL dose is not the regimen described for this scenario.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because hourly dosing for 12 hours is not the advised honey schedule.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because honey is given while awaiting removal, not only after the battery has passed the oesophagus.

sourceRefs: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
